text:
Nora H.: FYI — new guidance out today on cross-border workcations and short-term secondments. Key bits: PTO accrual treatment when you work >30 days in another country, mandatory local tax check for stays >45 days, and updated pre-travel checklist. Full: https://intranet.redwood.com/policies/cross-border-work

Mateo R.: Nice. For accruals: do we pause accruals or pro-rate?

Nora H.: We pro-rate accruals based on local employment rules. For hosted employees (US/UK/DE) accrual continues but may be adjusted for local statutory minimums. The policy page has a per-country table.

Jenna K.: What about health insurance and travel medical cover?

Nora H.: Company health coverage remains primary for approved short-term workcations up to 90 days. For >90 days you need to enroll in local cover or get People Ops approval for continued Redwood coverage. Emergency med evac options are in the travel checklist.

People Ops Bot: :bookmark: Policy posted: "Cross-border workcation & secondment guidance". Compliance tasks created for employees planning >30 days abroad. See policy link above.

Mateo R.: Will managers get a template to approve/deny secondments?

Nora H.: Yes 1-step manager form in Workday and a Manager TL;DR kit in #managers. We also added a short FAQ for contractors and interns.

Jenna K.: Any changes to expense or per-diem rules?

Nora H.: Per-diem unchanged. Travel expense rules now require a "local tax check" checkbox for reimbursements when travel spans countries. Details on the expense page.

Mateo R.: Thanks 1 can you flag any country exceptions?

Nora H.: Done 1 exceptions list is on the policy (countries where transfers or accrual adjustments are restricted). DM People Ops if youre planning something edge-case.
